output.methodChoice: D (competing hypotheses) with C-style IS/IS NOT splitting: several rival causes (price, connector, seasonality, app) coincide in time, and cohort data discriminates between them.
output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is not mainly a pricing problem. Since Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March, the Quillbook connector has silently dropped or doubled invoices. About 1,212 of 1,900 connected accounts were affected. Of those, 34% had cancelled by 31 July, against 8% of unaffected Quillbook accounts. Quillbook accounts churn at about 6% a month whether or not they were repriced. Accounts with no connector, which are most of the base, churn at about 1.9% a month, near the Q1 rate. That holds across seat bands, so the finance team's size pattern is explained by larger accounts using the connector. The health panel counts only errors, so it never showed the problem. Support response times also slowed.

Recommendation: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority and schedule it now. Contact every Quillbook account, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold, because it has kept 3,870 duplicate invoices out of customers' books. Do not roll back the price, which would cost about $220k a month and would not address the cause. Do not start the Tallymarsh rebuild yet. First review its log, since the numbers are tiny. I am fairly confident in this diagnosis (about 85%).
